body.summary: Friends at the Table's Marielda arc is a two-stage actual-play mini-season: a game of The Quiet Year builds the island city of Marielda in the year after Samothes tears it from the continent, then Blades in the Dark follows a crew of information-brokers, the Six, through heists in the reconfigured city fifteen years later. Their jobs escalate from stealing a train's route-plate to breaking into Memoriam College, and finally to helping Maelgwyn kill the god Samothes in the belief that his death will birth something to hold back the Heat and the Dark. ||The killing works but goes wrong: the wrong blade is used, Samothes's divinity is torn four ways, Maelgwyn becomes a bound replacement Samothes, and the city is pinned in place as the City of First Light.||

characters.name: Castille / Charter Castille
characters.role: protagonist, pala-din blacksmith and former mage
descriptors: marble pala-din body housing an elf mage's consciousness
floppy hat, turtleneck dress, obsidian scarring
cat figurine she can inhabit
later given flesh by Primo
relationships: Maelgwyn: wary friendship and flirtation, drinks and crossed fingers
Sige: crewmate she shocks with ghost-light when he attacks Maelgwyn
the mages of the University: former colleagues who knew her as Charter

characters.name: Sige Coleburn
descriptors: huge man, undercut, bare-knuckle-boxer dress
missing fingers from a factory accident
sawed-off holy gun and a trench knife
rebuilding a magic boat he never finishes
relationships: Samol: bargains with the earth-god to leave Marielda
Aubrey: gives her his modified gun, initials HKC scratched on it
Lance Noble Orchid: steals his gun twice

characters.name: Aubrey Zosim
descriptors: small bookish cobbin, twine-mended glasses, burn-scarred leathers
fire oil, smoke bombs, dream essence
haunted by visions of the mansion
relationships: Samot: dream-visitant who recruits her to do violence
Peg and Zaktrak: cobbin cohort who fuss over her
Sige: friendship sealed by the gifted gun

characters.name: Edmund Hitchcock
characters.role: protagonist, one of identical twin brothers (Slide)
descriptors: dashing ex-cavalry officer, blue jacket, gold braid
goes 'soft' after trauma
carries half a map to a mansion
relationships: Ethan Hitchcock: twin, lies to him about the plan
Samothes: prayed to him, shown the Heat and the Dark
Caroline and Carolyn Fair-Play: confused by the twin students

characters.name: Ethan Hitchcock
descriptors: same face as Edmund, cavalry boots that clank
believes they are recovering treasure
leaves with a candlestick
relationships: Edmund: twin he is kept in the dark by
Thackeray: rival whose nose he cut off

characters.name: Maelgwyn
descriptors: blond, masked, gauntleted hand
wears a mask of Samot's face and a crown
the blade in the dark grows with each kill
relationships: Samothes and Samot: their son, though he has forgotten
Castille: weekly drinks, awkward tenderness
the mages: his patrons and co-conspirators

characters.name: Samothes
descriptors: dark-skinned bearded god, humble robes, forge and anvil
reconfigures the city at will
makes a sword meant to save the world
relationships: Samot: estranged beloved, 'you're a fool and you're going to get us all killed'
Maelgwyn: son who kills him
Primo: his cobbin partner, the Artificer Mundane

characters.name: Samot
characters.role: god, the Boy-Traitor, god of books and wine
descriptors: blond, pale, shit-eating grin
goblet and book sigil
speaks to Aubrey in dreams
relationships: Samothes: lover and rival
Maelgwyn: son he urges toward regret
Aubrey: recruits her as 'my very own Primo'

characters.name: Samol
descriptors: slow drawl, 'ain't a thing I don't know'
tree-like, then a vast scaled sea-beast
dying of a sickness
relationships: Samothes and Samot: his sons
Sige: offers escape in exchange for stopping the Gardeners

characters.name: Primo
characters.role: the Artificer Mundane, Samothes's cobbin partner
descriptors: old cobbin, cloudy eyes, soot-blackened apron
tailor and inventor, big bed, corkboard of designs
invents a no-pee ray
relationships: Samothes: devoted working partner
Aubrey: recognizes 'good blood', gives her an apple

characters.name: Claret Holiday / Tamsyn
characters.role: leader of the Red Rank Irregulars
descriptors: dyed red hair, military jacket, saber
clean teeth
drains those near her
relationships: the Six: hires them for the Memoriam job, later allies in the Fontmen war

characters.name: Lance Sovereign Thackeray
descriptors: no nose, shimmering purple coat, cavalry boots
long-barreled pistol
relationships: Hitchcock: old rival who cut off his nose
Maelgwyn: killed by him on the train

characters.name: Hedy Braum / Other Hedy
descriptors: stretched taffy limbs, balloon-escape voice, toothy smile
found inside a tree
relationships: Sige: leads him to Samol in the woods
the Weaver Union: its advocate

characters.name: Rebecca, Lance Noble Orchid
descriptors: Fontman turned Lance Noble, scarred, mismatched new hand
cane that burns
relationships: Hitchcock: hand cut off by him
Castille: repeatedly propositioned at brunch

settings: Marielda / the City of First Light, an island torn from Hieron by Samothes
the parishes: Canopy Row/Orchid, the Gold Zone/Chrysanthemum, Helianthus, Iris, Quince, Violet, Emberboro
the volcano palace of Samothes and the Divine Forge
Memoriam College and the Winsley Cartwright Living Library

arcs.summary: The Quiet Year builds Marielda week by week: Tamsyn kills a rich boy, Hedy is found in a tree, the pala-din arrive, and the frost shepherds end the year.
arcs.locator: 01 The City of Light Pt. 1 through 02 The City of Light Pt. 2

arcs.summary: The Six rob the Crosstown Express for its route-plate, fighting the Golden Lance and losing Thackeray to Maelgwyn.
arcs.locator: 03 The Crosstown Job Pt. 1 through 04 The Crosstown Job Pt. 2

arcs.summary: Claret Holiday hires the crew to steal a book from Memoriam College; they find Bolster Valentine's ghost, the Yellow House, and Maelgwyn in a vault.
arcs.locator: 06 The Valentine Affair Pt. 1 through 09 The Valentine Affair Pt. 4

arcs.summary: The Six plan and carry out the killing of Samothes, which births a bound new god and pins Marielda in place.
arcs.locator: 11 The Killing of the King-God Samothes By The Traitor Prince Maelgwyn Pt. 1 through 14 The Killing of the King-God Samothes By The Traitor Prince Maelgwyn Pt. 4

motifs: the Heat and the Dark, and arguments over which comes first
the glowing lava-water ringing the island
maps and route-plates that steer reconfiguration
twins and doubled selves (the Hitchcocks, Caroline and Carolyn, Castille and Charter)
the blade in the dark that lengthens with each kill
apples from Nacre, gone from the city
ghosts in bottles and prisms that project memory
themes: gods as embodied emotions (confidence, regret, ingenuity)
gentrification and class across the parishes
found family and the cost of loyalty
irreversible mistakes in a world that can no longer rewrite history

notable_scenes.summary: Tamsyn beats a rich boy to death with a fire poker, and the city learns there is no law.
The pala-din walk out of the sea and the Quiet Year ends.
Hitchcock hangs from Thackeray's boots out the back of the train.
Bolster Valentine's ghost force-chokes Castille in the Hanging Gardens.
Sabinia shows Edmund the observatory view of Marielda burning at the edges.
Maelgwyn kills Samothes with the wrong blade, and the volcano shudders.
notable_scenes.locator: 14 The Killing of the King-God Samothes By The Traitor Prince Maelgwyn Pt. 4

notable_scenes.summary: Samol explains that the tomb was the artifact, and that he has seen the stars.
notable_scenes.locator: 14 The Killing of the King-God Samothes By The Traitor Prince Maelgwyn Pt. 4
